lines.text: This is your twenty twenty-five in music. Three hundred sixty-nine artists, nine hundred twenty songs, and one very loud year.
You listened for seventy-four thousand, six hundred fifty-eight minutes. That's almost fifty-two days of music, and you pressed play on three hundred forty-eight days of the year.
Your longest run: fifty days in a row, ending December seventh.
Your number one artist, for the second year running: The Warning. Over fifty-five hundred minutes. More than Led Zeppelin and AC/DC combined.
Right behind them, a classic-rock lineup: Led Zeppelin, AC/DC, Steve Miller Band, and Aerosmith.
And your song of the year: Rocket, by Def Leppard. Sixty-nine plays. Over seven hours of it.
Your sound was mostly hard rock, nearly a quarter of everything you played, with blues rock and alternative rock close behind. A hundred sixty-six genres in all.
And on June twenty-third, you played eighty-three different genres in a single day.
The eighties were your decade, with the seventies right on their heels.
You found eighty-four new artists, including Kacey Musgraves, Chuck Mangione, and Roberta Flack.
And between the songs, more than eleven hundred hours of podcasts, led by Tim Conway Junior.
Turn it up for twenty twenty-six.
